agree.reason: The arithmetic, the falling-ad comparison, the June checkpoint and the respectful plan for the 11-year ad seller give even the two ad-background members solid reasons to vote yes, but they may still ask why ads can't run alongside membership during the transition.

honest.reason: The numbers are accurate, and unknowns like retention are left as placeholders instead of being made up, but turning the pilot into "$20,350 a year" assumes nobody cancels, and "the model can carry well beyond what ads now bring us" leans on a 40% figure from another newsroom whose budget we don't know.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 35-a-week pilot pace, the 1.5% and 6% conversion rates, the 875 members needed and the 13-a-week pace against what the pilot already achieved, plus a checkpoint figure that matches, all correct and framed favourably.

right_comparison.reason: It correctly treats the $47k drop as happening in one year and projects a $37k–$54k range rather than a flat $84k, though the projection is labelled 2027 when the next step of the decline would land in 2026.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint names a date (30 June 2027), a number (545 members, about $52k) and a consequence (a revised budget and options at the July meeting), and it is tied to risks that really could go either way.

objections.reason: It deals with the staff member's role, the risk that the pilot only drew the keenest readers, and cancellations, but it never directly answers the ad-minded members' likely question of why ads must stop completely rather than run alongside membership for a while.

fit.reason: It is a clearly laid-out board memo with the decision up front, and at about 550 words it roughly fits on one page.
